title: The Four Princes Grow Up
captions: The four princes grew up together in the palace gardens: Rama, Lakshmana, Bharata and Shatrughna.
Lakshmana followed Rama everywhere like a shadow, and Shatrughna stayed close to Bharata. The four brothers loved one another dearly.
Each morning they went to their guru, the sage Vasishtha. They bowed to him and learned the holy scriptures with full attention.
They also learned to ride, to use the bow and to protect the weak. Rama's arrow always found its mark, yet he never boasted.
Every day the princes bowed to their father and mothers and asked for their blessings before anything else.
The people of Ayodhya adored them. Rama spoke kindly to everyone, rich or poor, and always stopped to help.
Then one day a great sage named Vishvamitra arrived at the palace. He had come to ask the king for something very precious.
story: The four princes of Ayodhya grew up together in the palace and its gardens. Rama was the eldest, son of Queen Kausalya. Bharata was the son of Queen Kaikeyi, and the twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna were the sons of Queen Sumitra.

The brothers loved one another dearly, and they paired up in a special way. Lakshmana followed Rama everywhere like his shadow, and Shatrughna stayed close to Bharata. Whatever one brother had, he wanted to share with the other.

Every morning the princes went to their guru, the sage Vasishtha. They bowed to him first, then sat down to learn the Vedas and the holy scriptures. They listened with full attention and asked good questions.

Their training did not stop with books. They learned to ride horses and elephants, to drive chariots and to use the bow. Rama became the finest archer of all, and his arrow always found its mark. Yet he never boasted, and he never made his brothers feel small.

Each day the princes bowed to their father and their three mothers and asked for their blessings. Rama spoke kindly to everyone in Ayodhya, rich or poor, and the people loved him for it. Then one day a great sage named Vishvamitra arrived at the palace gates, and the lives of the princes were about to change.
lesson: Rama and his brothers were princes, yet they bowed to their guru, listened carefully and served their parents every day. Being clever or strong is a gift, and vinaya means carrying that gift gently, without showing off. An old Sanskrit saying teaches that true learning gives humility. The more we know, the gentler we become.
lesson_long: Vinaya means humility: staying gentle and respectful, even when you are very good at something.

Rama was a prince, the best archer in the land, and loved by everyone. He could easily have become proud. Instead he bowed to his guru, served his parents and spoke kindly to all. An old Sanskrit saying teaches vidya dadati vinayam, which means true learning gives humility. The more we know, the gentler we become.
Our elders compare a wise and humble person to a tree full of fruit. The heavier the branches, the lower they bend.
tradition: In ancient India, children often lived and studied with their guru in a gurukula. They learned the scriptures, archery, music and good conduct together, and they served their teacher with respect. We still remember this bond on Guru Purnima, a festival day when students thank their teachers.

Bowing to elders and touching their feet is called pranam. When a child bows, the elder places a hand on the child's head and gives a blessing. It is a small act, but it shows that we know we still have much to learn.
words: a teacher who guides us, in learning and in life
the oldest holy scriptures of Hindu dharma
a school where students lived and learned with their guru
bowing to an elder with respect
question: What is something you are good at? How can you use it to help someone, without showing off?
questions: What is something you are good at? How can you use it to help someone, without showing off?
Rama never boasted about his archery. Why do you think people loved him for that?
What is one way you show respect to your teachers?
